title: Compact-root descent of a small cellular tree
statement: Use the universe, regularity, presentability, weak saturation, and $L$-tree definitions in [lem-coef-weak-saturation-tree-presentation]. Let $\tau$ be uncountable regular and $\mathcal A$ a locally $\tau$-presentable ordinary category: it has small Hom sets and all small colimits and is generated under small $\tau$-filtered colimits by a small family of $\tau$-presentable objects. Let $L$ be any arrow class whose sources and targets are $\tau$-presentable, and let $\{Y_t\}_{t\in T}$ be an $L$-tree with root $Z$, with $|T|<\tau$. There are $\tau$-presentable objects $M,N$, a map $M\to Z$, and an $L$-tree indexed by the same poset $T$ with root $M$ and colimit $N$, such that the original tree is isomorphic to its objectwise pushout along $M\to Z$. In particular the canonical square with top map $h:M\to N$ and bottom map $Z\to Y_T$ is a pushout, and $h$ lies in the weakly saturated closure of $L$. No assumption that $Z$ itself is presentable is required.
